title: Platform Seller Friction Map & One-Pagers (draft)
linked_artifacts: JIRA-PLAT-321: Dedicated vs Private decision flow
content:
Goal: give field platform sellers a single-sheet playset to diagnose buyer friction, quickly map to technical levers (latency/cost/reliability/routing), and deploy a one-page response for each common objection. Draft — rough, intentionally terse.

Top-level friction clusters (observed in Q4 demos / discovery calls):
1) Performance uncertainty: buyer worried about tail latency and p50-99 guarantees for synchronous chat endpoints.
   - seller signal: heavy emphasis on SLAs, live demo requests, ‘how do you guarantee 200ms?’. 
   - quick response (one-pager): show our SLA tiers + typical p50/p95 baseline for comparable models (sample snippet below), plus canary rollout + fallback explanation.
   - technical pointers: recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity for stable p95; show autoscale/burst policy notes.

2) Cost per request / pricing unpredictability: infra teams ask about per-token spikes, embedding costs.
   - seller signal: questions on caching, batching, quantization, reserved commits.
   - quick response: reference Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching + prefix caching) + reserved capacity calculator (link). One-pager includes math example for 1M messages/mo.

3) Data security & compliance friction: concerns about data residency, KMS integration, audit trails.
   - seller signal: legal asks for SOC2/ISO/contract language or wants on-prem.
   - quick response: two paths: Hosted with dedicated tenancy + KMS vs Private (VPC/on-prem) checklist. Attach compliance checklist.

4) Model quality/regression anxiety: product managers want deterministic output, regression rollback.
   - seller signal: ‘how do you prevent a model update from breaking prompts?’.
   - quick response: rollouts + evals: highlight per-prompt eval hooks, canary traffic split, automatic rollback triggers. One-pager shows minimal test matrix for a canary.

5) Integration inertia: teams refuse to re-architect cache/tokenization flows.
   - seller signal: ‘we can’t change our client architecture’.
   - quick response: SDK snippets, adapter examples, and a migration path: 1) proxy wrapper 2) sidecar inference 3) full SDK.

One-pager templates (each should be a printable single page, title + 3 bullets + evidence + TL;DR script):
A) Latency Assurance One-Pager
  - TL;DR script: “We’ve got 3 concrete knobs: reserved capacity for predictable p95, autoscale for burst, and lightweight model variants as fallback. We’ll canary to your production traffic and set rollback triggers.”
  - Evidence: sample numbers: p50 80ms, p95 240ms (dedicated c5-like baseline for 8k seq). Notes: numbers depend on model family/sequence length.
  - Technical checklist: model variant to pair, recommended GPU profile, required observability hooks (tracing header, token-level cost).

B) Cost Predictability One-Pager
  - TL;DR script: “We layer reserved commits with usage-based overflow. Optimize suggests batching + quantization — typical savings 30%–55% on token cost.”
  - Evidence: worked example for 1M chat turns, 80 tokens/turn — show monthly cost with and without batching.
  - Technical checklist: tagging tokens, enabling prefix cache, suggest quantization option (int8/4bit).

C) Compliance Pathway One-Pager
  - TL;DR script: “We’ll run a short readiness audit and map to Hosted Dedicated or Private. If you require on-prem, we offer an appliance cadence with sha'd binary and audit logs.”
  - Evidence: KMS integration steps, sample contract language, retention controls.
  - Technical checklist: network egress controls, HSM/KMS mapping, data deletion SLA.

D) Regression & Rollback One-Pager
  - TL;DR script: “We test new model variants against your golden prompts and run canary with auto-fallback to prior model on drift.”
  - Evidence: eval tooling screenshots (placeholder), A/B config sample.
  - Technical checklist: test prompt set, metrics to monitor (semantic-similarity drop, failure rate), rollback policy.

Quick objection scripts (for engineers/architects):
- Objection: ‘We can’t tolerate variability in latency.’
  Script: ‘Understood — let’s scope a dedicated capacity POC for a week with your 95th percentile traffic profile; we’ll instrument tracing and commit a rollback SLA in writing.’
- Objection: ‘Embedding costs blow up our budget.’
  Script: ‘We recommend an embedding cache + hybrid sparse vector store and a monthly commit with overflow pricing — here’s a cost model we can run with your sample dataset.’

POC checklist (minimal viable POC in 2 weeks):
Week 0: alignment doc, golden prompt set, traffic sample (1–2 days)
Week 1: deploy Dedicated trial cluster + baseline perf tests (3 days)
Week 2: run canary with 10–20% traffic + evaluate quality/regressions (4 days)
Success criteria: p95 within committed threshold, cost per 1k tokens within target, zero data egress violations.

Open questions / rough notes (to be resolved before next deck iteration):
- Can we publish a short micro-benchmark matrix for the subset of models we intend to ship as Recommended for Dedicated? (See github PR link in header)
- Get Legal to stamp the one-pager contract phrases (JIRA-LEGAL-78).
- Need quick internal script that shows impact of quantization on output fidelity for two customer prompts (owner: Marcus).

References and internal hooks:
- Eval harness: github.com/redwood-inference/evals (see run-canary.md)
- Pricing calc sheet: CONFLUENCE-PRICING-12
- Internal demo clip: slack://files/demo-latency-jan23

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep the one-pagers extremely visual — scoreboard + 3 bullets + 1 tiny chart. Engineers love single-number guarantees.
- We should fold in a tiny ‘how to scope’ checklist for solutions engineers — they need clear acceptance criteria to hand back to buyer.
- Remove heavy legal language from sales-facing doc; keep it in linked artifact.

Next steps for this draft:
- Convert one-pager templates into actual PDF/slide assets (owner: Jonah) — target 2026-02-12 for first pass.
- Validate sample perf numbers with Applied ML (owner: Priya) — due 2026-02-01.
- Run 2 internal roleplays with AE + SE using these scripts (owner: Elena) — schedule for 2026-02-08.

Appendix: quick benchmark snippets (paste-in for slides)
- command: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer -d '{"model":"rwd-4k","prompt":"<golden>","max_tokens":128}'
- metric: sample run: p50: 72ms, p95: 210ms, token-rate: 18k/s on ded-rtx-6000 baseline

End of draft — very rough. Use as working doc for next iteration.
